question: Which of the following describes the largest subset of values of \(y\) within the closed interval \([0, \pi]\) for which \[ \sin(x + y) \le \sin(x) + \sin(y) \] for every \(x\) between \(0\) and \(\pi,\) inclusive?
solution:
On \([0,\pi]\), sine is nonnegative and cosine is at most \(1\). These facts let us bound each term in the sine addition formula.

Take any \(x,y\in[0,\pi]\). Since \(\sin x\ge0\) and \(\sin y\ge0\),
\[
\sin x\cos y\le\sin x,
\qquad
\cos x\sin y\le\sin y.
\]
Adding these inequalities gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin(x+y)
&=\sin x\cos y+\cos x\sin y\\
&\le\sin x+\sin y.
\end{aligned}
\]
This works for every pair \(x,y\) in the given interval, including the endpoints. Therefore every allowed \(y\) works, so the largest subset is \(\boxed{0\le y\le\pi}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
